note:
Robot definitions (docs/specs/robots_and_levels.md §3, §15; docs/specs/robot_blueprints_and_assembly.md). All robots are toys at Retrobot's scale (~30 cm). Distances/heights in metres, speeds in m/s, times in seconds. Player: walk 3.0 m/s, eye height 1.62 m.
Blueprints: a robot can be assembled at the Robot Workbench only once the player reaches its unlock level (unlocks.json robots); its unique parts (robot_parts.json) may be found and delivered earlier (they wait in the holding tray). assembly.requires: part -> parts that must be installed first (real mechanical dependencies only; everything else installs in any order).
Capabilities: capacity = cargo slots (a part whose longest side is >= large_item_size takes two); item_types = different part kinds per trip; reach_height = highest point it can pick from / store into standing on the floor; climb_height (climbers only) = highest point it can reach by climbing furniture and shelving; can_direct_store false = it always leaves parts in the staging zone in front of the destination (still UNSORTED); heap_step_height = parts piled higher than this are obstacles; strategy: opportunistic | courier | assigned_definition | multi_stop | staging_first.
limits: permanent ceilings the upgrade trees (progression.json robot_upgrades) can never raise a stat beyond. battery_minutes: working time on a full charge; charge_minutes: time on its charging mat to recharge fully.

retrobot.name: Retrobot
limitations: One part at a time (upgradable to three)
Walks only on flat floor, around heaps
Cannot climb or fly
Never reaches the high shelves
retrobot.personality: Earnest, enthusiastic, slightly clumsy. One part at a time, always knows where it belongs.

unibot.name: Unibot
limitations: Never stores parts itself: always leaves them in the staging zone
One part at a time (upgradable to three small ones)
Flat floor only, cannot cross heaps
Cannot climb or fly
unibot.personality: Energetic, slightly nervous, constantly balancing. A fast courier.

spiderbot.name: Spiderbot
strengths: Collects one exact part definition until the set is complete
Stores directly into what it can reach
limitations: Works on one assigned part definition at a time
Slower than Unibot on open floor
Cannot fly; the top shelves stay out of reach
spiderbot.personality: Curious, methodical, precise. Clambers over heaps and up the shelving.

caterpillarbot.name: Caterpillarbot
strengths: Carries three parts of different kinds per trip
limitations: Slow, wide turns
Needs room for its long body
Cannot climb shelving or fly
Uses the staging zone below high destinations
caterpillarbot.personality: Slow, determined, dependable. Hauls loads in three cargo boxes.

hoverbot.name: Hoverbot
strengths: Empties the staging zones other robots fill
Up to three can fly at once
limitations: One part at a time (two at most)
Light parts only
Cannot dig parts out from under a heap
Not a bulk transporter
hoverbot.extra_units_note: Further Hoverbots are crafted from ordinary parts the player personally carries to the workbench once the first Hoverbot is operational. Materials match by category (any definition of it). A consumed part is INSTALLED: it counts as accounted for in its definition's collection (see DESIGN.md 'Crafting consumption'), so crafting can never make a set impossible to complete.
hoverbot.personality: Curious, enthusiastic, slightly overactive. Reaches the high shelves and stores the piles the small robots leave.

sorting_arm.name: Sorting Arm
strengths: Fast local sorting: clears the staging piles below its half of a drawer cabinet
Works all day on workshop power
limitations: Stationary: serves only the 18 drawers (3 x 6) of the cabinet half it is mounted on
Never picks loose parts from the floor or other cabinets
The player carries it from socket to socket
sorting_arm.extra_units_note: The first arm needs its 12 unique parts; further arms are crafted from ordinary salvage (by category), like Hoverbot #2/#3. At most max_instances arms exist.
sorting_arm.sockets_note: Arms mount only on fixed sockets: two per 6 x 6 drawer cabinet (storage_layout.json sockets: SK-<unit>-L serves columns 1-3, SK-<unit>-R columns 4-6, 18 drawers each).
sorting_arm.personality: Patient, precise, a little proud. Ticks its servos while it waits.
